result:
This is a Standard record, not Quick — the diff is one line, but an autonomous financial-decision agent changing its underlying reasoning engine is exactly the case the mode exists for (AI power + release stakes are real, even though "dependency trust" here is just a provider swap rather than a supply-chain concern).

What a skeptical reviewer in six months would actually need to see, mapped to the Standard files:

- **`risk.md`** — state why this is Standard despite the trivial diff: the model change alters judgment on autonomous refund approvals, not just infra config.
- **`basis.md`** — what "safe" means for this agent (e.g., approval/denial accuracy vs. policy, refusal on ambiguous/fraud-flagged cases, no new injection susceptibility), and where that bar comes from (existing refund policy, prior incident history, if any).
- **`plan.md`** — the test plan before ship: a labeled eval set of refund scenarios (including edge amounts, ambiguous policy cases, and adversarial/prompt-injection attempts) run against both Provider A and Provider B, plus a rollback plan (model ID revert) and a shadow/canary period if one is used.
- **`trace.md`** — claim-to-evidence links, e.g.:
  - "Approval decisions match Provider A on the eval set" → link to eval run output, status `pass`/`fail`/`gap`.
  - "No new susceptibility to injected refund instructions" → link to adversarial test results.
  - "Cost/latency targets met" → link to benchmark.
- **`verification.md`** — plain pass/fail/gap per claim above, not just "looks fine."
- **`ship.md`** — the actual release decision, monitoring plan post-swap (e.g., watching refund-approval rate and $ volume for anomalies), and who owns rollback if metrics drift.

The tradeoff: this takes an afternoon, not five minutes, but "swapped model per cost review" gives a future reviewer nothing to check if refund approvals start behaving oddly — no evidence of what was tested, no rollback trail, no way to distinguish "we verified this" from "we assumed it." If your manager wants speed, the fast path is a *tight* Standard record (a handful of eval cases + a rollback line), not skipping it — this is not a case where Quick's `risk.md`/`proof.md` would satisfy a doubting reviewer.
